publication: Bartosz Jan Bednarczyk and Ian Pratt-Hartmann, Computational perspectives on the classical decision problem, ESSLLI 2026 Lecture 2: The monadic fragment, Prague August 10, 2026. Lecture delivered by Bednarczyk; slide footer credits both course lecturers.

reviews.checked_passages: Logical slides3–7, expanded PDF pages27–71: unary profiles, equality-free collapse, need for multiplicities with equality, capped representatives and assignment/witness preservation.
reviews.consumers: Monadic logic: matching profile capacities, both witness directions, quantifier-count invariance, small models and terminating finite search.
reviews.outcome: BPH-MON-01: zero-quantifier/zero-constant bound must be made positive for nonempty models. The corpus proves max(1,q)2^k for sentences without constants and expands the source proof outline. Tiling reductions, complexity lower bounds and later fragments are outside this review.
